Art Directors at Riot drive the quality and performance of their team, establishing direction and goals that provide clarity and focus. Your scope of responsibilities include leading with vision, strategic partnership across the game, a deep understanding of audience resonance, overall team culture and performance, growth of your direct reports, and directing your team on successful execution of your vision and strategy.

As an Art Director an unpublished R&D product, you will help bring the game’s visual direction to life in a new game for players around the world. You will translate our creative direction into a distinctive, emotionally compelling, production-ready visual identity that supports gameplay, strengthens character appeal, and meets the craft bar players expect from Riot. You will partner closely with Creative Direction, Game Leadership, cross-disciplinary teams, and external partners to translate the game’s visual ambition into a cohesive, art direction. 

Responsibilities:

  • Steward the game’s visual identity from concept through production
  • Translate creative direction into clear visual standards, production practices, and scalable art workflows
  • Drive visual quality, appeal, and gameplay readability across all player-facing art
  • Apply deep expertise in the art style across art, animation, VFX, visual storytelling, and character-driven experiences
  • Balance artistic ambition with technical requirements and production realities
  • Build, lead, and mentor high-performing internal and external art teams
  • Direct co-development partners, vendors, and distributed creative talent to deliver consistently high-quality work
  • Partner across design, narrative, audio, engineering, product, and IP to ensure art strengthens the player experience
  • Provide clear visual feedback through reviews, paintovers, references, and development guidance
  • Maintain deep awareness of the art style, creative influences, and evolving player expectations

Required Qualifications: 

  • 12+ years of experience developing games, with 8+ years leading art teams
  • Experience as an Art Director or key artistic decision maker on at least one shipped 3D game
  • Experience delivering games with strong character appeal in both model and animation
  • Strong understanding of the pipelines, production techniques, and technical constraints required to deliver stylized visuals in games
  • Strong artistic judgment across character design, composition, shape language, color, lighting, animation, VFX, and gameplay readability
  • Experience balancing visual quality against technical, production, platform, and team-size constraints
  • Experience building, leading, mentoring, and aligning art teams across cross-functional game development
  • Experience directing external vendors or distributed art teams
  • Champion of healthy creative processes that support iteration, alignment, scalable production, and strong artistic quality
  • Experience leveraging emerging technologies and workflows, to accelerate visual development while maintaining artistic quality, authorship, and creative integrity
  • A portfolio demonstrating strong artistic judgment, visual clarity, compositional skill, and stylistic range
  • Experience developing games in modern game engines (i.e. Unreal, Unity, etc)

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience developing art direction for live-service, multiplayer, or other technically constrained games
  • Experience with 3D games that place high demands on character appeal, animation, VFX, camera, gameplay readability, or combat clarity
  • Working knowledge of stylized rendering techniques, VFX, animation, and visual clarity for gameplay

For this role, you'll find success through craft expertise and a collaborative spirit that prioritizes the delight of players. We will look at your past studies and experience, but for this role, we also look for dedicated people with a personal relationship with games. If you embody player empathy and care about players' experiences, this is the role for you!

Riot’s Anti-Cheat team is versatile and passionate about its craft. We understand the player impact of cheating in games and are focused on setting the highest bar for the integrity of multiplayer games. We relish the opportunity to work with low-level systems and take pride in developing creative, rigorous defenses against adversaries. At the most fundamental level, our goal is to promote the best player experience by protecting the legitimacy of their favorite games.

As a Manager, Anti-Cheat Engineering, you will lead the team responsible for the ongoing development and evolution of Vanguard Anti-Cheat’s Windows client services. You’ll set technical direction, shape priorities, and ensure the team delivers secure, reliable capabilities across Vanguard’s Anti-Cheat suite in a timely manner. While your primary focus will be enabling the team and driving outcomes, your strong fluency in cheat communities and techniques will allow you to guide architecture, challenge technical decisions, and step directly into complex debugging or investigations when needed. You’ll help the team anticipate and analyze emerging cheat techniques, then translate those findings into effective detections, mitigations, and preventative controls. 

Responsibilities:

  • Manage, identify, recruit, interview, and hire engineers to help the team scale effectively
  • Set direction and drive high-impact anti-cheat capabilities from ambiguity through production across user-mode, kernel-mode, and obfuscation tooling surfaces
  • Lead the team in rapidly translating emerging threats into resilient detections and preventative countermeasures that can be safely deployed at scale
  • Balance immediate threat response with proactive technical investments that anticipate adversaries’ next moves or eliminate common abuse vectors entirely
  • Guide and participate in complex investigations involving highly evasive cheats and operating-system manipulation techniques
  • Ensure the team can diagnose and resolve complex compatibility, reliability, and security issues in highly opaque environments, stepping into the details when needed
  • Build trusted relationships with game teams as internal customers, helping them understand their cheating ecosystems, integrate Anti-Cheat effectively, and make informed tradeoffs across security, player experience, scope, and delivery
  • Establish clear priorities and technical expectations, helping engineers navigate uncertainty and make sound decisions across security, compatibility, performance, and operational risk
  • Partner across engineering, product, operations, and game teams to align dependencies, communicate risk, and deliver anti-cheat capabilities successfully across Riot’s portfolio

Required Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience leading product or developing engineers, either as an Engineering Manager or as a Technical Product Lead
  • Familiarity with cheat-development or game-security research communities and a practical understanding of modern cheat techniques and anti-cheat evasions
  • Strong understanding of Anti-Cheat architectures, with the ability to evaluate designs, guide technical discussions, and engage directly when complex problems require it
  • Experience leading work on low-level, security-sensitive systems and helping teams navigate tradeoffs across security, reliability, compatibility, performance, and delivery
  • Working knowledge of Windows security model and security feature suite such as Secure Boot, HVCI, and measured boot attestation

Desired Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with reverse-engineering techniques and workflows, including the analysis of packed, protected, or obfuscated binaries, with the judgment to translate technical findings into priorities, investments, and defensive strategy
  • Working knowledge of the Windows kernel and driver model, sufficient enough to guide architecture, assess technical risk, and oversee the development and operation of production-grade kernel-mode drivers
  • Working knowledge of advanced evasion techniques involving hypervisors, DKOM, EPT manipulation, vulnerable drivers, or hardware-assisted cheats, with the ability to reason about their implications for product and technical strategy
  • Basic understanding of runtime integrity verification, behavioral detection, client attestation, and other signature-less anti-cheat techniques, including how to prioritize investments across these defensive approaches
  • Experience balancing near-term responses to emerging threats with longer-term, proactive investments intended to anticipate how adversaries and the broader security landscape will evolve
  • Experience partnering with internal customers, building trusted relationships, translating their needs into technical priorities, and leading productive conversations around scope, risk, sequencing, and delivery tradeoffs

For this role, you'll find success through craft expertise, a collaborative spirit, and decision-making that prioritizes the delight of players. We will be looking at your past studies, experience, and your personal relationship with games. If you embody player empathy and care about players' experiences, this could be your role!

As a Staff Full-Stack Software Engineer specializing in AI, you will personally design and build the AI agent capabilities and product experiences for an internal enterprise intelligence platform. This includes the retrieval, orchestration, and reasoning layer that sits on top of a semantic data layer built and maintained by a partner data engineering team. You’ll turn these capabilities into search, chat, and workflow experiences that help leaders find information and make decisions faster. This is a hands-on, coding-majority role. You’ll build the agents, prompts, tool integrations, and full-stack product surface yourself.

  • Instrument AI features with observability for quality, latency, token usage, and cost, and use it to drive iteration and tuning. 
  • Iterate on prompts and model choices quickly, with sensible fallback behavior when a model, tool, or retrieval step fails or returns low-confidence output. 
  • Apply solid engineering fundamentals: source control, code review, automated testing (unit, integration, functional), CI/CD, and on-call for the systems you own.

Required Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field (or equivalent professional experience delivering enterprise technology solutions). 
  • 8+ years of professional experience in full-stack software development 
  • Practical, end-to-end experience building RAG or agentic systems: retrieval, tool-calling, structured outputs, multi-step reasoning, and verification/evaluation loops, not just familiarity with LLM APIs. 
  • Experience designing and running evaluation approaches for nondeterministic systems: curated datasets, automated metrics, human review, and production feedback.
  • Experience establishing basic AI observability (quality, safety, reliability, latency, token usage, cost) for features you build. 
  • Working understanding of AI security and responsible-use risks, prompt injection, tool abuse, data leakage, access control, model limitations, sufficient to build safeguards into what you ship. 
  • Deep hands-on programming experience in Node, TypeScript, React. 
  • Experience with modern frameworks (e.g., NextJS, NestJS). 
  • Experience building RESTful and GraphQL APIs, working with relational (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL) and non-relational (e.g., Redis) databases. 
  • Comfortable with cloud infrastructure and deployment: AWS, containers (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), CI/CD pipelines. 
  • Familiar with software engineering best practices: automated testing, code review, monitoring/observability, security and performance considerations.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Deep practical knowledge of retrieval-augmented generation and semantic search, including embedding and reranking models, retrieval design, grounding, citations, and evaluation. 
  • Experience with agent platforms (e.g., LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, or comparable), vector databases, and multi-agent orchestration patterns. 
  • Working familiarity with Python and lakehouse/data-catalog concepts (e.g., Databricks, Unity Catalog), enough to collaborate effectively with the data engineering team, without needing to own pipeline build-out.
